messages:
Aisha Bello: pushed the draft overload protection dashboard panels + initial alert thresholds. would love eyes esp on paging vs noise. link: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/overload-protection/hosted-overload-protection (staging)

Aisha Bello: key new panels: shed_rate by (region, model), breaker_state transitions, runtime queue depth, p99 latency, 429/503 breakdown. alerts currently:
- breaker_open_ratio > 0.15 for 5m (page)
- shed_rate > 0.10 for 10m (page)
- queue_depth_p95 > 0.80 of max for 5m (page)
- 429_rate > 0.05 for 15m (ticket)

Sergio Costa: looking now. initial reaction: breaker_open_ratio alert at 5m is gonna flap during canary + during autoscale ramp. suggest page on sustained open OR on rapid transitions.

Allison Grant: +1. also would strongly prefer multi-window burn alerts over single 5m window. 5m spikes are expected when we *want* shedding to engage.

Rafael Mendes: we need to be careful: if shedding is working, we shouldn’t page just because shed_rate is high. we should page when control plane is unhealthy OR breaker isn’t recovering.

Christine Wong: agree. shed_rate itself is not inherently bad. how about “shed_rate high *and* p99 latency high” OR “shed_rate high *and* breaker open > X for > Y” to catch “stuck open”.

Tomáš Novák: also think we should separate: customer impact vs platform risk. platform risk = routing timeouts, runtime oom, queue blowups. customer impact = % requests shed. both useful, only some page-worthy.

Sergio Costa: on the dashboard: can we add an annotation line when breaker transitions happen? like “CB_OPEN” and “CB_CLOSE” markers. makes it easier to correlate with latency + errors.

Aisha Bello: yep, can add the transition events graph as an annotation source. the breaker service emits `breaker_transition_total{to_state=...}`.

Logan Wright: metric label note: please do NOT add customer_id/tenant_id to any of these panels. keep it to region/model/tier/route_class. we already got burned on cardinality last quarter.

Caleb Johnson: tracing side: are we planning to sample overload spans differently? if shed_rate spikes, traces blow up unless sampling adjusts.

Allison Grant: on alerting, my suggestions:
1) replace breaker_open_ratio > 0.15/5m page with:
   - `breaker_open_ratio > 0.30 for 30m` => page (stuck open)
   - `breaker_transition_rate{to_state="open"} > N` in 10m => ticket/notify (possible flapping)
2) shed_rate alert should be ticket by default unless paired with latency regression.
3) queue_depth is good, but use p95 queue time or scheduler backlog too (depth alone can be noisy w/ long prompts).

Rafael Mendes: +1 on “stuck open”. during canary we expect open/half-open behavior as we dial thresholds. paging will train people to ignore.

Christine Wong: for “flapping” detector: we can do `transitions_total{to_state="open"} + transitions_total{to_state="half_open"} > 20 in 15m` and page only if also `shed_rate` oscillates. otherwise ticket.

Sergio Costa: also, do we want different thresholds by tier? premium tier should probably get tighter page triggers if they’re seeing sustained 503.

Aisha Bello: i can split by `tier` label. current panels have tier filter but alerts are aggregate. question: do we page on premium-only impact even if overall is fine?

Sean Gallagher: yes, but keep it simple: page if premium tier has sustained elevated *internal* failures. shedding (429/503 overload-protected) is expected, but we should still watch for sustained “no capacity” scenarios.

Nora Ahmed: for messaging, can we add a panel that distinguishes “overload-protected errors” vs “internal 5xx”? support keeps escalating when they see 503s even when they’re the new expected shape.

Aisha Bello: already have a draft panel: `http_responses_total` broken out by `error_class` = {overload_protected, internal_error}. it relies on slo-toolkit mapping from PR-204.

Grafana Bot: Sergio Costa shared a dashboard snapshot: https://grafana.redwood.internal/render/d-solo/overload-protection/hosted-overload-protection?panelId=42

Sergio Costa: the 429/503 breakdown panel is good. but alert “429_rate > 5% for 15m” will fire constantly during game day and any real overload event. I’d make it “notify only” and tie paging to user-visible SLA breach (p99 or error budget burn).

Allison Grant: exactly. we should alert on *burn*:
- fast burn: 2% budget in 1h
- slow burn: 5% in 6h
and treat overload-protected separately. if overload-protected burns budget, that’s a product decision; but it shouldn’t page as ‘incident’ unless it violates documented behavior.

Rafael Mendes: action items:
- Aisha/Sergio: adjust alert rules per above (stuck open, flapping detector, shed+latency correlation)
- Allison/Logan: review metric naming + label set one more time before we ship to prod
- Nora: draft one-liner for support: “shed engaged; not an internal outage” + when to escalate

Aisha Bello: got it. will update alerts:
- page: `breaker_open_ratio{tier="premium"} > 0.30 for 30m` AND `routing_5xx_rate_internal > 1%` OR `p99_latency > SLO`
- ticket: transition_rate high (flap)
- notify: shed_rate high without latency regression

Christine Wong: can you also add cooldown/hysteresis metrics to the dashboard? e.g. `breaker_cooldown_active` or time-since-last-transition. helps debug “why isn’t it closing”.

Aisha Bello: yes. we have `breaker_state_age_seconds` from the routing service. I’ll add a panel.

Caleb Johnson: last thing: sampling. if shed decisions become frequent, we should sample only a fraction of “admitted=false” traces, otherwise trace volume spikes exactly when infra is stressed.

Logan Wright: +1. we can do head-based sampling rule: keep 1% of shed spans, 10% of half-open probes, 100% of internal errors. will follow up in #observability.

Tomáš Novák: :thumbsup: once alerts updated, can we run a small replay from perf-canary overload scenario and see which alerts would have fired? we want “0 pages” on expected shedding.

Aisha Bello: yep, will do after I update the rule set. will post results here.
